how_do_i_tame_a_horse_black_mesa_named_n.card_text:
--- Local knowledge base (bonsAI; offline corpus; may be truncated) ---
Domain: strategy

[Black Mesa / mechanic: Starting out in Black Mesa] (trust: wiki_no_patch)
Black Mesa is Half-Life rebuilt from the ground up on the Source engine, with new art, sound and voice work but the original's chapters, weapons and enemies kept on purpose rather than added to. The one exception is Xen: those chapters are mostly new work and far longer than the 1998 originals, so budget more time for the alien world than veterans remember. Expect the same shape of game throughout: no cutscenes, scripted scenes you walk through, a crowbar for crates and vents, and fights that go better from a doorway than from the middle of a room. There are 25 achievements, Workshop support and a separate deathmatch mode; the campaign itself is single-player only.

[Black Mesa / mechanic: The opening tram ride and where it leads] (trust: wiki_no_patch)
Black Mesa opens with a long tram ride that needs no input beyond looking around; it carries you from the surface entrance through checkpoints and cargo bays into the underground facility, and doubles as an unskippable loading screen for the level ahead. Step off at the platform, badge through the checkpoint, and follow the corridor signs to the locker room, where you change into the orange HEV suit before the day's work — the path there is linear, so a door that will not open yet is one you have not reached the switch for. Anomalous Materials, the lab down the following hall, is where the real gameplay opens up: once things go wrong there, the crowbar on the floor nearby is the first weapon in the game, and from then on every locked vent or wooden crate is worth swinging at before hunting for another way around.

[Black Mesa / enemy: Houndeye] (trust: wiki_no_patch)
Three-legged with one big compound eye, and always in a pack of up to four. Alone one is timid; together they charge a sonic shockwave that hurts you and smashes crates and glass, and the damage rises with the size of the pack. Kill the leader and the rest lose the ability to charge the wave and fall back to a weak bark, so pick out the one the others follow. A resting pack dozes and wakes to noise, which is your chance to line up the first shot. Bullsquids leave them alone, so a room with both is not a three-way fight.

--- End local knowledge base ---

[Hades / mechanic: Darkness, keys and gems] (trust: fallback_no_source)

Early on, keys and Darkness are both bottlenecks — take whichever you have fewer of, and stop taking gems once the contractor jobs you want are bought.

[Black Mesa / boss: Gonarch] (trust: wiki_no_patch)
The giant four-legged headcrab mother in the caverns of Xen. Its shell shrugs off almost everything; the pale egg sac swinging under its body is the only part that takes damage, so any shot not at the sac is wasted. At range it lobs white acid mortars from its back, up close its front legs slash for huge damage, and whenever it sees you it births baby headcrabs in pairs, up to twenty alive at once: weak and fast, there to distract you from the sac. It walks the webbing over the pits that you and its children fall straight through, so watch your footing more than its feet. When it dies the sac bursts and releases one last brood, so back away before the pop.

how_do_i_beat_the_bone_hydra_in_hades_ha.card_text:
--- Local knowledge base (bonsAI; offline corpus; may be truncated) ---
Domain: strategy

[Hades / mechanic: Weapon choice] (trust: fallback_no_source)
Take the Stygian Blade first: it is the most forgiving of the six and asks the least of you. The Shield of Chaos is the next easiest, because holding block turns a mistake into nothing. Of the rest, the Eternal Spear is the safest, since its reach keeps you out of trouble. Leave the Twin Fists of Malphon until later — they are the fastest, but they need you standing inside everything. The Heart-Seeking Bow and the Adamant Rail both want range and punish standing still, and the Rail can leave you reloading at the worst possible moment.

[Hades / boss: Theseus and Asterius] (trust: fallback_no_source)
Two at once, which is the actual difficulty. Asterius, the bull, telegraphs a long charge — sidestep it and he is briefly stuck. Theseus throws his spear and periodically calls down a god's power, which is marked on the ground before it lands. Most runs go better killing Asterius first, because Theseus alone is predictable.

[Hades / mechanic: Heat and the Pact of Punishment] (trust: fallback_no_source)
Beating the game once is the middle of the story, not the end — the runs continue and the ending needs several more. The Pact of Punishment unlocks then too: Heat is optional difficulty you add yourself, in exchange for rewards that only come from raising it.

--- End local knowledge base ---

--- Local knowledge base (bonsAI; offline corpus; may be truncated) ---
Domain: strategy

[Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor / boss: Glyphid Dreadnought] (trust: fallback_no_source)
Kite between waves; focus weak-point armor plates as they open. Save overclock/nuke for armor break windows.

[Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor / boss: Dreadnought Twins] (trust: fallback_no_source)
Summary: Two smaller Dreadnoughts at once - the Lacerator chases and leaps, the Arbalest hangs back firing fireball spreads.
Weak points: Neither is as tough as a full Dreadnought on its own.
Phases: Let their health bars drift apart and both turn immune while they heal the gap closed.
Tips: Split fire evenly rather than burning one down, and the healing never starts.

[Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor / enemy: Exploder] (trust: fallback_no_source)
Summary: Large orange glyphids that walk into you and detonate in a wide blast.
Weak points: Fragile, and the blasts chain, so one popped early clears the group behind it.
Tips: Weapons fire themselves, so it dies where you stand - keep distance and the blast lands in the swarm instead.

--- End local knowledge base ---

[Portal 2 / mechanic: Excursion Funnel] (trust: wiki_no_patch)
Weightless travel along the beam. If it is carrying you the wrong way, look for the button that reverses it before assuming the route is shut. It passes through portals, so it can cross the whole chamber, and it ferries gel and cubes as well as you.

[Portal 2 / mechanic: Co-op portals and pinging] (trust: wiki_no_patch)
Two players, two guns, four portals — and a portal one of you places links with the other's, which is the whole puzzle most of the time. Ping to point at a spot or to count down a timed jump; it carries without voice chat. Dying costs nothing but seconds.

[Portal 2 / boss: Wheatley] (trust: wiki_no_patch)
He strips the portal surfaces, shields himself and throws bombs. Let a bomb break the conversion gel pipe, paint a wall with what spills, and portal his own bombs back into him. Every stun buys time to attach one corrupted core; three of them force the transfer.
